St. Abraham the Righteous

St. Abraham the Patriarch · St. Righteous Forefather Abraham · Abram

Period
Biblical patriarchal period; no independently established absolute dates assigned here
Region
Mesopotamia; Canaan
Titles / vocation
Righteous · Patriarch
Commemoration

Introduction

St. Abraham is the biblical patriarch called from his country to receive God’s promise of descendants, land and blessing for the nations.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeathCommemoration and biblical legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Death in old age in Genesis 25:7–10; no martyrdom described

Read circumstances and sources

Background

Genesis introduces St. Abraham under the earlier name Abram. God calls him to leave his country and kindred and go to a land that God will show him. The promise concerns a people and a blessing extending beyond his own household; he travels to Canaan in response.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Genesis 11:27–12:9

Life and notable events

God confirms the covenant and changes his name to Abraham. His story includes receiving visitors at Mamre, interceding for a threatened city, and becoming the father of St. Isaac in old age. In Genesis 22 he takes Isaac to the place appointed for sacrifice; God stops the killing and provides a ram. Hebrews later presents this trial as an example of trust in God’s power to fulfill the promise.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Genesis 17:1–8; 18:1–33; 21:1–5; 22:1–19; Hebrews 11:17–19

Death

Genesis reports that St. Abraham dies at 175 years of age and is buried in the cave of Machpelah. This is the biblical lifespan, rather than an independently dated modern chronology. The narrative does not describe martyrdom.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Genesis 25:7–10

Commemoration and biblical legacy

The OCA commemorates St. Abraham on October 9 and also among the Holy Forefathers before the Nativity. The latter observance is movable, occurring on the Sunday falling between December 11 and 17 in the church calendar.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Commemoration heading and final paragraph · [3] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Opening explanation of the Sunday

Romans 4 explains his faith in relation to God’s promise. Matthew places him at the beginning of Christ’s genealogy.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Romans 4:1–25; Matthew 1:1–2
